remaining_gaps: Not decided. The sixteen committee continuations in Section 1-101 (each continued until December 31, 1982) and Sections 1-102 through 1-105 need a clause-by-clause inventory and first-end check. Held later instruments that reach it are Executive Orders 12299, 12305, 12336 and 12399, but the dossier records unresolved whole-versus-partial readings for 12299 and 12336, no provision of Executive Order 12345 was located, and the effective date of each partial revocation was not settled in this run. No claim is filed.

Not decided. The order corrects typographical errors in Sections 1-101(h) and 1-101(o) of Executive Order No. 12258, so each clause continues only as long as the corrected provision; the first end of each therefore depends on the unfinished first-end determination for those committee entries of Executive Order No. 12258 (the dossier lists Executive Orders 12336 and 12399 as possible actors with no located provision). No claim is filed.

The order specifies January 21, 1981 as the hostage return date for sections 101(2)(A) and 205(b)(1) of the Hostage Relief Act of 1980. The held OFR 1989 Codification prints it as in force on 1989-01-20 and no ending instrument is held. Missing sources: the text and later history of the Hostage Relief Act of 1980 provisions the specification serves (5 U.S.C. 5561 note) and any later order or statute that ended or exhausted the specification.

The clause inventory and own terms are read: the order establishes an emergency board (United Transportation Union and National Carriers Conference Committee dispute, 1985) and Section 4 says the board terminates upon submission of its report; the first end of the board and of the report and standstill provisions therefore turns on the date the report was submitted, which is not held. No held source records the report date or the end of the standstill, and the packet lookup of held texts for this order number found only its own text, so no express revocation is held either. Missing source: the board's report to the President with its submission date (National Mediation Board record) or a held later order revoking this one.

Executive Order No. 12610 is held and states that Executive Order No. 12534 is superseded, with a stated effective date, but earlier partial ends were not excluded. No claim is filed.

The order amends Executive Order No. 12528 to raise the Board to 35 members and to provide that the Board terminates on July 1, 1989 unless sooner extended. Executive Order No. 12692 (September 29, 1989, effective September 30, 1989) revokes Executive Order No. 12528 as amended, but that is only an upper bound: the own-terms date July 1, 1989 may be earlier. Missing sources: the text of Executive Order No. 12528 and evidence whether the Board was extended or terminated on July 1, 1989.

Section 4 terminates the Task Force 30 days after it submits its report, and Section 2(b), as amended by Executive Order No. 12621, sets the report deadline. The date the report was submitted is not held, so the termination date cannot be computed, and no revocation is held. Missing source: the Task Force report with its submission date, or a held later order ending it.

The order uses the Armed Forces to restore law and order near Atlanta, Georgia until the Secretary of Defense determines under Section 4 that forces are withdrawn. No held source records the withdrawal determination or date, and Proclamation 5748 is not held. Missing sources: the Secretary of Defense withdrawal determination (or a record of the withdrawal date) and Proclamation 5748.

The order delegates functions vested in the President by H.J. Res. 523 as enacted April 1, 1988, which is not held, so the sections of that Act under which the delegations operate, and when its transfer and designation authority lapsed, cannot be checked. No later instrument is held. Missing source: the text of the Act (H.J. Res. 523 of 1988) with its time limits, or a later order revoking the delegations.
